grid.source: Nine supplied architectural PDFs; filenames 1–9. Drawing numbers differ from filename numbers.
grid.status: Architectural reference — sourced grids and heights; schematic undimensioned shapes.
assumptions: Grid coordinates and stated elevations are dimension driven; all render views share one geometry.

Tower face width 4.900 m follows the facade witness chain, distinct from its 5.889 m grid zone. Upper-stage taper, cap radii/curves, moulding projections, niche contours and cross widths are illustrative profiles, not measured dimensions.
Tower cross apex follows the explicit +36.920 m level; the separate cap segment chain closes 1 mm higher.

The entrance clear widths follow 2.150 / 3.100 / 2.150 m from the plan; wider decorative surrounds remain schematic. The facade recess is a plan-traced proxy. Explicit clear nave length 47.386 m is recorded in the workbook but its unresolved face offsets are not claimed as exact in this mesh.
The 9–10 side-gable roof ridge and its valley intersections are visual proxies, not an approved roof-junction detail.

Inner C/G wall faces are set to Z ±7.250 m for the explicit 14.500 m clear width, using a derived 0.220 m centered wall proxy; wall build-up is unconfirmed. Column diameters, other wall thicknesses, reveals, stair count, rails and finials are illustrative.
The paired exterior windows and large exterior doorways use detail-sheet nominal width and height references; detailed profiles and corner junctions need CAD review.
The two outer verandas remain open circulation spaces, with separate inner and exterior opening layers.

Pews, decorative lighting, stained-glass colors, altar furnishings and interior finishes are visual proposals. No engineering sizing, installation details or equipment quantities are inferred from these visual elements.
No detached rear annex or lower rear roof: the primary longitudinal gable continues to axis 12.

Two side sanctuary doorways connect +0.160 m to the −0.320 m veranda using visible illustrative threshold treads. Floor datums and doorway positions are sourced; tread runs and counts require an architectural detail.
Interior fit-out is a concept proposal: pews, kneelers, altar furniture, reredos, devotional artwork, glazing colour, chandeliers and sconces are not specified by the supplied architectural PDFs.

Main clear nave width 14.500 m, structural grids, source column heights and the continuous timber-supported roof topology are retained. Added timber lining and member profiles are illustrative; no Gothic vault or new ceiling volume is introduced.

The centre aisle and side aisle routes remain clear between the seating blocks. Cross aisles are kept at the principal side-door bays. This is not an occupancy, accessible-route or egress certification.

The existing source-derived sanctuary floor is +0.800 m. Furnishings are positioned on that level; the altar, ambo and reredos dimensions are visual design choices requiring parish and architect approval.
The reredos is a proposed furnishing in front of the existing separation at axis 11. It does not establish the missing architectural elevation or room-wall height.

The five dynamic lights provide a responsive day/evening visualization. Their intensities are uncalibrated image settings; no lighting performance, electrical load, equipment quantity or installation detail is inferred.
Stained-glazing patterns and Stations of the Cross frames show proposed decorative locations. Artwork and sculpture are visual placeholders for a later commissioned design.

The central facade above +8.45 m follows the church’s CAD file of 23 October 2026 (DWG sheet 1, E01B; plans at +10.128 and +15.840 m): upper storey with a triple window and rose, side niches with pedestals, fleur-de-lis cresting, pinnacled piers and a niche aedicule with a cross on a disc to +24.648 m. Faces and levels are traced; moulding profiles and carving are illustrative.

The side porches follow the parish priest’s decision of 25 October 2026: no outer wall, concrete columns on the B/H axes with two-centred pointed arcade and cross arches, a guard except where the outside stairs land, doors and windows only in the inner C/G wall, a cast roof slab under the tiles and plain walls closing the 9–10 side bays from the porches. The 9–10 C/G arch intrados uses four native circular arcs and the short impost shelves from CAD detail 47 (26 October audit); its display band/depth and the porch column, arch, guard and beam sizes remain proposals on engineering hold.

Fourteen Stations of the Cross, one per nave bay between the columns above the window or door, with a candle light pair below (parish priest, 25 October 2026). Frames and relief are placeholders for commissioned artwork.

Tower bases and tops follow the church’s CAD file of 23 October 2026 (E01B, plan sheet 5) at the owner’s direction of 25 October 2026. The 26 October native-entity audit corrects the six upper-front assemblies and the six outer-side assemblies to native arch/window/rose coordinates; twelve inner/rear assemblies repeat that coordinated profile as DERIVED pending elevation confirmation, the ground front arch radii, offset-circle dome shoulders to +32.790457, adjoining lantern levels and the trefoil cross outline to +36.919970. The parapet now has 17 native stepped openings per face, source rail/cornice profile rows and finials to +31.551771; 60 mm plan-band separation is only a display-depth proxy with structural thickness null. Existing coloured rose finish, wall X planes and all equipment positions are retained. The E02 outer ground face has its distinct +3.100470 blind arch and 1 m opening; rear/inner elevation identity, the ET stage-2 rose discrepancy, parapet structural section and corner/depth interpretation, relief depth, hidden dome continuation, revolution, blade angles, glazing and construction sections remain unverified. The stage-1 wall plane stays at X 0; ISSUE-R06 unit confirmation stays open.

Exterior roofline audited against DWG version 23102026: E02 parapet top +7.073919; EW outside wing rose +7.571529 and cross +15.186895; E03 rear rose +9.988501 and cross +17.829188. Source circular niche arches, rose boundaries, mitred cornices and cross silhouettes are transcribed; depths, capital/pinnacle carving, tracery and scrolls remain visualization proxies. Roof elevations and fixture positions remain; display roof ends are trimmed to the current gable face planes. ISSUE-R05 ridge and ISSUE-R06 units remain open; not for construction.

Lower pilasters at both wing ends and the sanctuary end follow the EW/E03 source shaft widths and heights; their projected depths, bases, capitals, fluting and connection to the existing plinth are concepts, not a structural design. Existing equipment and routes remain in place; access, weatherproofing and engineering holds remain open.

Main plinth 22.489 m and projecting wing plinth 28.158 m use the plan overall witnesses. Structural axes and the 2.835 m projection per side remain fixed. Front stage stays within 27.254 m tower facade width and 1.600 m above courtyard. Detailed face offsets remain provisional.

Exterior side doors now occupy the same outer wall plane as the windows, following the latest user correction. Doors open in Walk mode. Tower front arches remain open with the existing rear wall plane visible beyond.

The sanctuary frame uses the three-lobed central and side arch silhouettes from section sheet 5. Curvature, relief depth and placement at axis 10 remain visual reconstructions pending a detailed longitudinal section.

Side access follows the plan and the corrected side reference: paired flights at the first doorway, single flights flanking the projecting bay. Stair count, tread run, balustrade profiles and exact landing edges are proposed.

Ivory plaster, stone trim, terracotta tiles, rubble plinth and timber shafts follow the selected images. The finishes are proposed. Two rows of eight trees, lawn and tree-bed soil are unsurveyed presentation concepts; grading, planting, drainage and circulation require site design.

Sanctuary revised from the approved concept and section sheet 5: the three-lobed frame stands on the axis-10 columns in lacquered timber, without a tie beam, and its side arches open into passages, and the Marian and Joseph shrines stand at the back of those passages in the side arches of axis 11, level with the crucifix (parish priest, 25 October 2026), with 2.2 m service entrances below raised niches. A timber-lined chamber with a gilded boarded vault runs from the frame back to the reredos on axis 11, where the crucifix stands in a niche 1.0 m deep that opens through the back wall onto a base over the service room. The bay behind each shrine is closed in lacquered timber above the shelf, and every round column on the D/E lines is lacquered: the nave columns have turned bases on panelled stone pedestals, carved capitals, junction blocks and dies with gilded lotus panels, and the two frame columns keep gilded bands and capitals. The tie beams, side beams, rafters, purlins, ridge and braces take the same lacquer, with gilded lines and bosses on the nave rafters and ridge; the boarded roof lining stays ivory. The reredos, chamber, shrines and front frame carry generated gilded relief, crocketed pinnacles and leaf crestings after the 7 October interior views; the niches are blue with a soft glow, the corpus is carved wood with a gilded cloth and the tabernacle is gilded under a dome. Member sizes, the roof thrust on axis 10 and the relief are proposals within the retained building grids.

Decoration surface study: mineral plaster, honed stone, satin red lacquer and gold-leaf roughness. Display-only maps, not measured optical/acoustic materials or selected construction products; geometry, equipment, routes and engineering holds unchanged.

Timber frame now follows section sheet 4 as measured on the vector PDF: main tie beam +8.59…+9.18 m (0.59 m deep), side beams +6.66…+7.00 m from the C/G piers to the D/E shafts, purlins about 0.50 m apart. The earlier king posts, diagonal braces and knee braces were not on the drawing and are now an optional "proposed bracing" layer.

Lengthwise beams on the D and E column lines (axes 3 to 10, 14 members, IDs B03-D-03-04 to B03-E-09-10) follow the owner-confirmed arrangement of the beam specification. Their 0.24 × 0.45 m section at +8.73…+9.18 m is a visualization proxy on engineering hold; no equipment is mounted on them. Carved haunches, cartouches and beam ends are applied ornament from the approved concept art and carry nothing. No haunch stands under the axis-9 tie beam, where the ambo key light and the presider light hang close to the columns.

steps.title: 01 · Survey and coordinate
steps.task: Check grid, floor datum, equipment positions and all concealed routes against the measured building. Use the circuit sheets to record corrections.
steps.hold: Survey and coordinated light, sound, air, access and concealment review must precede physical setting-out. This default layout still has unmet targets.

steps.title: 02 · Boards and feeder paths
steps.task: Review DB-1 to DB-2, LC-1, FC-1 and AV-1 paths. Confirm enclosure access and the proposed supply/control separation.
steps.hold: Electrical designer: supply, phases, earthing, fault level, protection, cable sizes, board capacity and final single-line diagram are pending. Do not energize from this model.

steps.title: 03 · Coordinate concealed containment
steps.task: Review all shared corridors and individual branches together. Select each run for its vertices and height; compare with structure and finished surfaces before closing any cover.
steps.hold: Containment size, power/signal separation, fixings, fire stopping, access panels and penetrations require coordinated approval. Coloured routes are enlarged display lines, not cable diameters.

steps.title: 04 · Lighting routes and fittings
steps.task: Review each light circuit and its LC-1 or DB-2 supply. Check chandelier support, aim, driver access, fan-blade interaction and labels against the matching paper sheet.
steps.hold: Selected-product photometry, support design, control channels, dimming compatibility and installation details remain pending. Review current per-seat lighting failures in the matching calculation report.

steps.title: 05 · Sound and microphone connections
steps.task: Trace speaker and microphone lines to AV-1 separately from rack mains. Review polarity, intended zones, furniture/floor interfaces and service access.
steps.hold: Amplifier topology, impedance/line voltage, connectors, shielding and separation are pending. Passive speaker ratings are not mains loads; feedback and wing clarity targets remain unmet.

steps.title: 06 · Fans and ventilation
steps.task: Review FC-1 and DB-2 routes, motor control compatibility and air paths with the lighting and sound systems. Keep the central processional view clear of visible fans and supports.
steps.hold: Current geometry is a study, not an accepted fan installation. Mounting, guards/clearance, duty points, make-up air, noise, concealment and maintenance access need specialist approval.

steps.title: 07 · Exit signs and required safety functions
steps.task: Identify E1 separately from discretionary light scenes. Coordinate the required emergency system, operating labels and test access with the responsible designer.
steps.hold: Emergency supply, duration, coverage and failure behavior are not established by the simulator. No scene or walkthrough step authorizes isolation of required safety functions.

steps.title: 08 · Powered decoration and interfaces
steps.task: Review decorative loads and concealed feeds, heat dissipation, isolation and replacement access without obstructing worship or other systems.
steps.hold: Final products, loads, supports, material/fire compatibility and control interfaces need approval. Empty stages may occur in edited layouts.

steps.title: 09 · Inspect, test and hand over
steps.task: After approved installation, the responsible team must record electrical verification, manual/scene and failure tests, light/sound/air measurements, as-built IDs and maintenance instructions.
steps.hold: No commissioning or construction approval is recorded here. Progress through these review steps does not release a hold or mark any work installed.
